about: The differences between the pinned Plane schema and this crate's document that were decided (issue #58, scripts/check-openapi.sh). One entry per oasdiff check and text, with the operations it holds on. An entry that matches nothing on one of its operations is STALE and fails the check, as an entry of exceptions.yaml does; a difference that no entry covers fails it too. `ref` is the record of the decision.

accepted.reason: A project with no cover answers `cover_image_url: null`. The pin's schema calls it a non-nullable string and sends null all the same; the owner chose to reproduce the behaviour, and this document says what is sent.

A project the caller sees only because it is public answers `member_role: null`. The pin's schema calls it a non-nullable integer and sends null all the same: its view annotates `member_role` with a subquery over the caller's own active ProjectMember row, which is NULL for a caller who has none (apps/api/plane/api/views/project.py:128-133, tag oracle/v1-pin-20261018), and its serializer declares `IntegerField(read_only=True)` (serializers/project.py:222). This is recorded as well as read: in the corpus's `non-member-lists-a-public-project` and `non-member-detail-of-a-public-project` the seeded `member`, who is in `ORA` only, gets `member_role: null` for the public project that the owner made and 15 for `ORA`; Thrust sends the same (the corpus comparison passes on both). The owner confirmed reproducing it on 2026-11-16. The same defect as EX-006's `cover_image_url`.

A person who is not a member of the project has no place among its members, so `sort_order` is `null` where the list has it. The pin's schema calls it a non-nullable number and sends null all the same: its list annotates `sort_order` with a subquery over the caller's own ProjectMember row (apps/api/plane/api/views/project.py:173-181, tag oracle/v1-pin-20261018), NULL for a caller who has none, and its serializer declares `FloatField(read_only=True)` (serializers/project.py:221). Recorded as well as read: `non-member-lists-a-public-project` has `sort_order: null` for the two public projects that the seeded `member` is not in (`PUB` and `WTY`) and 65535.0 for `ORA`, which they are in. A one-project answer has no `sort_order` key at all (every list row of the corpus has it and no one-project answer does, `non-member-detail-of-a-public-project` included), so for the operations that are not a list the finding is about the declared schema; the document lists the key as optional. Thrust sends the same (the corpus comparison passes on them). The owner confirmed reproducing it on 2026-11-16. The same defect as EX-006's `cover_image_url`.

A body that is a form is a 415: Thrust reads JSON only (`request::json_body`). The pin also reads forms. The owner confirmed this on 2026-11-07 for projects and on 2026-11-16 for every v1 route, to be revisited if a real client sends a form (D-030 (5)).
A body that is multipart is a 415, as a form is (D-030 (5)).

The pin writes `network` as `allOf: [NetworkEnum]` with Django's column range 0 to 32767 beside it; this document states the enum directly. Both say 0 or 2. oasdiff reports the form at warning level (the next three entries are the same difference).
`network` is the enum 0 or 2 here and in the pin's `NetworkEnum`; oasdiff does not see through the pin's allOf (SD-006).
The pin's 32767 is the range of the column; the enum is the constraint (SD-006).
The pin's 0 is the range of the column; the enum is the constraint (SD-006).

A body that is a form is a 415 on a state, as on a project (D-030 (5)): Thrust reads JSON only (`request::json_body`, one condition for every v1 route). The pin also reads forms. The owner confirmed D-030 (5) for projects on 2026-11-07 and for every v1 route on 2026-11-16; D-031 (5) is it, on the states.
A body that is multipart is a 415, as a form is (SD-010).

The pin's schema gives `slug` the pattern `^[-a-zA-Z0-9_]+$` (the validator of a `SlugField`), and the pin does not keep to it: `State.save()` stores `slugify(name)` in a field that is `blank=True`, and a name of CJK or emoji alone has the empty slug on the pin and here (D-031 (2), owner confirmed). This document does not claim a pattern, because the route can send an empty slug (`tests/openapi.rs`, `a_name_with_no_letter_has_an_empty_slug_which_the_document_does_not_forbid`).

A body that is a form is a 415 on a label, as on a project (D-030 (5)) and a state (D-031 (5)): Thrust reads JSON only (`request::json_body`, one condition for every v1 route). The pin also reads forms. The owner confirmed D-030 (5) for projects on 2026-11-07 and for every v1 route on 2026-11-16; D-032 (6) is it, on the labels, and `a_form_or_a_multipart_body_is_a_415` in `tests/labels.rs` holds the behaviour.
A body that is multipart is a 415, as a form is (SD-013).

A body that is a form is a 415 on a work item, as on a project (D-030 (5)), a state (D-031 (5)) and a label (D-032 (6)): Thrust reads JSON only (`request::json_body`, one condition for every v1 route, and both families of paths share the handlers). The pin also reads forms. The owner confirmed D-030 (5) for projects on 2026-11-07 and for every v1 route on 2026-11-16; D-033 (11) is it, on the work items, and `a_form_or_a_multipart_body_is_a_415` in `tests/work_items.rs` holds the behaviour.
A body that is multipart is a 415, as a form is (SD-015).

accepted.ref: the pin's schema, not a deviation (the oracle's corpus, work_items.json, the exchange `search`)
accepted.reason: The pin's schema gives the search answer the six required keys of ONE hit (`IssueSearch`: `id`, `name`, `project__identifier`, `project_id`, `sequence_id`, `workspace__slug`). Its recorded answer is `{"issues": [hit, ...]}`, with `sequence_id` a whole number where the schema says a string (the corpus's `search`), and this document describes that (`IssueSearchDto`), which is what Thrust answers too (`a_search_finds_what_a_name_an_identifier_or_a_number_says` in `tests/work_items.rs`). The six findings are the six keys that the answer does not have at its top level.

accepted.ref: the pin's schema, not a deviation (D-033 (5); the corpus's `list-expand-assignees-labels-state`)
accepted.text_contains: StateRef, subschema #2` to the `state` response property
accepted.reason: The pin's schema says `state` is a uuid. With `expand=state` its routes answer the state's four keys instead (the corpus's `list-expand-assignees-labels-state`), and so do these (D-033 (5)), so the document says both: the id, or `StateBriefDto`. oasdiff reports a oneOf added to the property here and a change of its type in the next entry. `assignees` and `labels` are the same (an id or the object) and are not in the pin's `Issue` schema at all, so oasdiff has nothing to say of them.

accepted.ref: the pin's schema, not a deviation (D-033 (5); the corpus's `list-expand-assignees-labels-state`)
accepted.text_contains: the `state` response's property `type/format` changed from `string, null/uuid` to `any`
accepted.reason: The same difference as SD-018: oasdiff reads a oneOf as the type `any`.

accepted.ref: the pin's schema, not a deviation (research/0014: the list's single-object mode)
accepted.text_contains: the response body was restructured into a oneOf
accepted.reason: With both halves of an integration key (`external_id` and `external_source`) the list answers the one work item that has it, not a page, as the pin's view does (`a_key_in_the_query_makes_the_list_the_one_work_item_that_has_it`). The pin's schema describes only the page, so the document says both (`Listing<IssueDto>`). oasdiff does not look inside a oneOf, so the rows of a page are compared through the operations that answer one `IssueDto` (retrieve, create, update), which share the type.

accepted.ref: range, not a behaviour a request can reach (`WorkItem.sequence_id` is an i64)
accepted.reason: The pin's column is an int32, so its schema bounds `sequence_id` to -2147483648 to 2147483647. Here the project's running number is an i64 and the document claims no bound. A project would have to make two thousand million work items for the two to differ.
